_comment: C0-17 正文英译 · udio（2026-10-26）。无附加小节。正文「相关条目」3 行带 .md 链接（suno/minimax-audio/runway），related 写 3 条（frontmatter related 是 [suno, elevenlabs, runway]，键按正文链接行对齐=3——minimax-audio 行在正文但不在 frontmatter）。sources 5 条对齐 frontmatter。runs 带「实测建议」三条段。

axes.model_access: A self-developed model line (v1/v1.5/v1.5 Allegro — the official FAQ names the currently available models); the new platform will train new models on "licensed and permitted music" (UMG official announcement narrative). Open-weights line: no official statement verified.
axes.runtime: Web (udio.com); generation on the vendor's cloud. There was once a Discord beta entry (community-history narrative, current status not verified item by item).
axes.local_files: Works stored on the account-side cloud; **the new platform heads toward a "walled garden" — the official announcement states AI-generated music cannot be downloaded/distributed outside the platform** (UMG announcement narrative); download rights during the transition follow the current ToS (not verified item by item).
axes.background: Generation is task-based (submit → queue → account library); no "keep-running-after-shutdown" form stated — tasks run in the cloud, independent of your machine being online.
axes.tools: Generation/extend/remix/Styles and other creation tools (named in the official FAQ); the new platform's direction is remix/covers/new creation experiences with participating artists' voices and styles (WMG announcement narrative).
axes.context: Task-based with no conversation memory; style continuity relies on Styles and similar mechanisms — reusable style presets are not memory.
axes.permissions: **The copyright settlements are the key background for understanding Udio**: June 2024 the RIAA sued on behalf of UMG/Sony/WMG; 2025-10-29 settlement + licensing deal with UMG (official announcement direct-fetched), 2025-11-19 settlement with WMG (official announcement direct-fetched), Merlin/Kobalt and others following (third-party industry-media reports, not verified item by item); the Sony lawsuit is ongoing (third-party narrative). Output rights shift with the transition ToS and the new platform's terms — always check the current ToS version before commercial use.
axes.fit: Fits: the creation experience of one half of music generation's two titans (reputation for complex genres), tracking the new licensed-platform form. Does not fit: commercial pipelines that need "download and take it with you" (the walled-garden direction), wanting settled terms (transition period).

runs:
This site has not completed measured runs. The coding-oriented test protocol is at [protocols/coding/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/coding/_protocol.md) (the coding task suite does not apply to creation products).

**Suggested measurements** (three, all pointing at things the official readable pages do not give):

- **The commercial boundary of current downloads under the transition ToS** (read the ToS original clause by clause)
- **v1.5 Allegro vs Suno v6 on the same prompt** (genre complexity/vocal naturalness)
- **Account/work migration after the new platform (Starstruck narrative) launches**
unknowns:
- The new platform's launch time and feature surface (official narrative says within 2026, specifics unset)
- The Sony lawsuit's direction (third-party narrative, no judgment verified)
- Transition-period download-rights details (ToS not verified item by item)
- The Discord entry's current status (not verified)
related: The other half of music generation's two titans: the two companies' lawsuit/settlement lines are independent, and their terms head in different directions.
Also audio generation: MiniMax runs speech/music dual lines, Udio focuses on music.
Audio-visual up/downstream: soundtracks generated by Udio often feed Runway-class video platforms for scored shorts (cross-linked after filing).
